What is the supremum of the function $y=f(x)$ shown above?

${sup}_{x\in R}f(x)=$
{{field-1}}
question.worked_solution:
The supremum of a function is the supremum of the range of the function.

In this case, the range of $f$ is $A=(-2,3].$

To find the supremum of a set $A,$ we must find the set containing **all** upper bounds of $A$ (i.e., the set of upper bounds) and take the minimum of this set.

So, in our case, we have that

- any number $y\ge 3$ is an upper bound of $A,$

- any number $y<3$ cannot be an upper bound of $A$ because $3,$ an element of $A,$ is greater than $y.$

Therefore, $[3,\infty )$ is the set of upper bounds of $A,$ and

$$
{sup}_{x\in R}f(x)=sup(A)=min[3,\infty )=3.
$$
